title: Modular Properties of Generalised Gibbs Ensembles: The Deformed KdV Hierarchy
abstract: We construct a set of conserved charges which are deformations of quantum KdV charges. They are associated with the modular transformation of a GGE with the spin-$σ$ KdV charge inserted with chemical potential $α_σ$. The charges are formal power series in the chemical potential, with coefficients given by local integrals of motion. We define local recursion relations and equivalent flow equations, prove commutativity to all orders, and establish uniqueness of the currents modulo total derivatives for a fixed generating series. We show that the eigenvalues of these deformed charges can be obtained from the thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz in two models. In the $c=1/2$ free fermion theory, the deformed charges reduce to explicit linear combinations of undeformed KdV charges, and their ground-state eigenvalues agree with the TBA expansion to all orders. In the Lee-Yang model, we find numerical agreement through cubic order in the spin-$5$ deformation for the first few charges evaluated on low-lying states.
summary: This theoretical work constructs and analyzes deformed conserved charges associated with the modular transformation of a Generalized Gibbs Ensemble in 2D CFTs. By proving the infinite-order commutativity of these charges and matching their eigenvalues to the TBA results in specific models, the paper provides a powerful tool for studying integrable dynamics far from equilibrium.
main_problem: The paper investigates the modular transformation of a Generalized Gibbs Ensemble (GGE) when a deformed KdV charge is inserted, aiming to understand the resulting conserved charges.
main_result: The authors constructed deformed KdV charges whose commutativity was proven to all orders in the chemical potential expansion. They showed that in the free fermion theory, these charges match the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) expansion to all orders.
method: The methodology involves constructing conserved charges as formal power series in the chemical potential ($\alpha$) derived from the asymptotic modular transformation of the GGE, and verifying their commutation relations.
model_or_system: The study is set in the context of a 2D Conformal Field Theory (CFT) described by a GGE. Specific models tested include the $c=1/2$ free fermion theory and the Lee-Yang model.
key_observables: Deformed KdV charges, ground-state eigenvalues, and the coefficients of the TBA expansion.
important_parameters: Chemical potential ($\alpha$), central charge ($c$), and the deformation parameter ($\sigma$ or $\kappa$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the asymptotic (perturbative) regime in the chemical potential, and the results are treated as formal power series, ignoring non-perturbative contributions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the modular transformation of the GGE trace involving defect insertions. Table 4 presents numerical values of the calculated eigenvalues for various charges across different low-lying states.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the deformed KdV hierarchy via the modular transformation of the GGE. It then proves the commutativity of these charges using recursion relations. Finally, it applies this framework to calculate eigenvalues in specific models, namely the free fermion theory and the Lee-Yang model.
why_interesting: The connection between integrable structures (KdV hierarchy), quantum statistical ensembles (GGE), and exact solvability methods (TBA) is highly relevant for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum many-body systems.
